convertibility_reason: Uses only built-in iFractals indicator with simple breakout entry logic, fixed SL/TP, and basic position management. No external libraries or custom indicators required.

derived_values.name: Upper Fractal Level (resistance)
derived_values.formula: iHigh(symbol, timeframe, Highest high among bars where iFractals returns upper fractal)
derived_values.used_by: Long entry breakout price, Short stop loss

derived_values.name: Lower Fractal Level (support)
derived_values.formula: iLow(symbol, timeframe, Lowest low among bars where iFractals returns lower fractal)
derived_values.used_by: Short entry breakout price, Long stop loss

other_exits: Stop loss and take profit are the only exit mechanisms; no signal-based closes

custom_logic_notes: Fractal levels are scanned backwards from bar 3 to a configurable lookback depth (Bars_Process). The highest upper fractal and lowest lower fractal found in this range become the breakout levels. A breakout above the upper fractal triggers a buy; a breakout below the lower fractal triggers a sell. SL for long is placed at the lower fractal level (or adjusted to meet minimum StopLevel); SL for short is placed at the upper fractal level (or adjusted similarly). TP is calculated as a fixed pip offset from the entry price. If the fractal-based SL would be too close (violating broker minimum stop level), it is adjusted outward to comply.
python_conversion_notes: Fractal detection must be reimplemented: scan recent bars to find bars where the high is greater than the 2 bars on each side (upper fractal) or low is less than the 2 bars on each side (lower fractal). Track the highest upper fractal and lowest lower fractal over the lookback window. Entry on breakout of these levels. SL/TP pip values need digit-adjustment logic for 5-digit vs 4-digit brokers. New-bar guard is essential to avoid duplicate entries. Position check (no existing trade) must be enforced before each entry.
